from.place: The proof requires gluing equivariant module sections.

title: Gluing equivariant module sections
statement:
theorem Scheme.GaloisCover.equivariantModulePresheaf_isSheaf
    {V : Scheme.{u}} (ℓ : ℕ) (P : Type u) [Group P] [Finite P]
    (c : Scheme.GaloisCover (ULift.{u + 1} P) V) (N : Rep.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ) P) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf V.smallEtaleTopology
      (c.equivariantModulePresheaf ℓ N ⋙ ModuleCat.restrictScalars
        (ULift.ringEquiv.toRingHom : ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ) →+* ZMod ℓ))

proof.text: Use the continuous-function sheaf after pulling back along the torsor. Etale base change continuity and composition of sheaves give a sheaf of continuous functions on the pullback.

Impose local equivariance as a subfunctor. The pullback universal property makes the condition stable under restriction; separatedness of the continuous-function sheaf shows equivariance is local, so the subfunctor is a sheaf.

Identify the underlying presheaf of equivariantModulePresheaf with the equivariance subfunctor by a natural isomorphism between locally constant and continuous functions for the discrete carrier. Transport the sheaf condition across this isomorphism and reflect it through the module forgetful functor using its limit instances. Restriction of scalars along ULift.ringEquiv leaves the underlying functions and restriction maps unchanged; reflection is through the forgetful functor for modules over ULift(ZMod ell).

old_proof.text: Give the representation carrier the discrete topology. Form the type-valued presheaf H by precomposing Scheme.Etale.continuousMapSheaf on c.P with MorphismProperty.Over.pullback along c.π and forgetting abelian groups. Etale.isContinuous_overPullback and Functor.op_comp_isSheaf_of_isSheaf prove H is a sheaf. This reuses the existing library construction of the continuous-function sheaf instead of reconstructing pointwise gluing.

Define the private equivarianceSubfunctor of H by s(action(g,x)) = rho(g)(s(x)). The pullback universal property proves that sectionRestriction commutes with sectionAction, so the condition is stable under restrictions. Given a section locally in the subfunctor, compare s composed with action(g) with rho(g) composed with s. Both are continuous (the representation carrier is discrete), and restrictions agree by local equivariance and the commutation identity. Separatedness of H proves equality, so equivariance is local. Apply Mathlib Subfunctor.isSheaf_iff to obtain the sheaf condition for the equivariant continuous functions.

Construct the natural isomorphism from the underlying type presheaf of equivariantModulePresheaf to equivarianceSubfunctor.toFunctor. Its forward map turns locally constant functions into continuous functions and its inverse uses IsLocallyConstant.iff_continuous for the discrete carrier. Both inverses are pointwise identities; naturality follows from pullback.hom_ext identifying sectionRestriction with the base-change functor map. Transport the type-valued sheaf condition along this isomorphism. Reflect it through the module forgetful functor using explicit HasLimitsOfSize, PreservesLimitsOfSize and ReflectsLimitsOfSize instances. The coefficient ring ZMod ell has universe zero, so ModuleCat.hasLimitsOfSize uses universe arguments (u, u+1, u+1, 0).
